- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.65) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high for 3–7 days.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ 0.05) over 3+ days, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 5–10 days.  
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply 1–2% downward adjustment for days 1–7.  
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecast days are above 10% above recent 10-day average, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.30) triggers downward correction: reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3–7 days.  
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 2+ consecutive days, apply downward bias of 1–3% per day until convergence.  
- For sentiment history with high volatility (e.g., alternating +0.67 and -0.30), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days to catch momentum.
